paper.title: Wang, Yu & Perdikaris (2020 preprint), When and why PINNs fail to train: A neural tangent kernel perspective
paper.scope: Independent small Poisson rod adaptation: empirical finite-width NTK with mean-normalised output blocks; single hidden layer width32, not original width100/500 or wave benchmarks. Fixed-step SGD with an initial empirical spectral heuristic is not a global stability guarantee or infinite-width convergence proof.

sources.name: Wang, Yu & Perdikaris (2020 preprint), When and why PINNs fail to train: A neural tangent kernel perspective
sources.text: Sections3–6 introduce the PINN kernel, spectral training dynamics and trace-based loss weights; Algorithm1. Our finite width32 rod uses mean-normalised Jacobian blocks, a smaller grid and2400 SGD steps; not the original wide-network or wave benchmarks.

sources.name: Primary HTML: kernel blocks and Algorithm1
sources.text: We distinguish empirical finite-network measurements from the paper’s infinite-width constant-kernel limit. Positive weights are analysed in symmetric weighted coordinates; trace balance does not establish equality of all convergence modes.

sources.name: Nine executed CPU controls, saved kernels and failed development pilot
sources.text: Three paired seeds, unit weights, frozen initial-trace weights and weights refreshed every400 steps. Complete final fields, kernel drift and initial-kernel continuous-flow diagnostics are retained; the earlier unstable pilot is separately disclosed.
